app.title: Peptide Fragmenter
app.summary: A person types a peptide sequence, which can include modification masses, and sets the charge range, the mass type, the fragment ion types and whether to include internal fragments. The interface checks the input, then works out every fragment ion. It shows them as one table per charge and as a plot of fragment segments against m/z, and the full fragment list can be downloaded. On a second tab the person pastes a measured peak list and sets a match tolerance and a minimum intensity. They get back an annotated spectrum, two match scores, a table showing which predicted ions were found, and a downloadable CSV of the matched peaks.

task.text: Calculate the theoretical fragment ions of a peptide and check how well a measured fragment spectrum matches them.

data.text: An amino acid sequence with optional modification masses, the predicted fragment ions computed from it, and a pasted peak list of m/z and intensity pairs from a measured spectrum.
data.item: a fragment ion of the peptide (ion type, position, charge, m/z), or a peak in the measured spectrum

stage.text: checking a measured fragment spectrum against a peptide's predicted ions, after acquisition

mechanism.text: Sidebar inputs drive the whole page: whenever the sequence or a parameter changes, the fragment tables and the segment plot are recomputed. On the Spectra tab, a pasted peak list is matched against the same fragments within a tolerance. The result is a bar chart with matched peaks coloured and labelled by ion type, two scores, and a combined ion table with the matched cells highlighted.

field.text: in silico peptide fragmentation and fragment spectrum matching in mass spectrometry

workflow.name: predict theoretical values and match them against a measured signal

steps.here: Type a peptide sequence with modification masses in parentheses and terminal ones in square brackets. The sequence is checked for valid residues, numeric modification masses and a residue limit. Then set the min and max charge, monoisotopic or average mass, the a/b/c/x/y/z ion types and internal fragments.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Every fragment ion's m/z is calculated and laid out as one table per charge. Residues are rows, ion types are columns colour-coded by type, and positions are counted from both termini.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A segment plot draws each terminal fragment as a vertical line at its m/z, spanning the residues it covers.

steps.step: bring the measured data in and set the matching rules
steps.here: On the Spectra tab, paste a peak list with one 'm/z intensity' pair per line, choose a tolerance in th or ppm, and set a minimum intensity. Peaks at or below the minimum are dropped.

steps.step: match predictions to measurements within a tolerance
steps.here: Each peak is matched to the fragment with the smallest error. In the bar chart, matched peaks are coloured by ion type and labelled with charge, type and number; hovering shows the charge, error and fragment sequence.

steps.step: score the match and see which predictions were found
steps.here: A hyperscore and a binomial score are shown. A combined table of ions by type and charge highlights the matched terminal ions in yellow and the matched internal ions in magenta.
The full fragment list downloads as fragment_ions.csv, and the matched peak list as spectra_results.csv.

distinctive: The sequence can carry modification masses in parentheses and terminal ones in square brackets, and these shift the fragment masses.
Tolerance can be absolute (th) or relative (ppm), and its default, step and maximum change with the unit chosen.
Fragments are numbered from the N-terminus for a/b/c ions and from the C-terminus for x/y/z ions, and internal fragments are optional.
The settings can be preset from URL query parameters, so a configuration can be bookmarked or shared.
A Wiki tab and a Help tab explain fragmentation methods and ion types alongside the tool.

parts.summary: Takes the peptide sequence and the fragmentation parameters, and stops with an error if the sequence, a modification or the charge range is invalid.

parts.title: Results tab
parts.summary: Computes all fragment ions from the settings and shows them, with an expandable full data table and a CSV download.
